sourceChecks.scope: Normative classifications and explicitly listed standard-pronunciation variants only. Does not establish learner analogies to Spanish, all modern phonetic realizations, articulatory measurements for every consonant, or the article’s unsourced example judgments.

sourceChecks.sourceTitle: Why are Korean tense stops acquired so early: The role of acoustic properties
sourceChecks.organization: Lee, S., & Lee, S. (2011), Journal of Phonetics; open full text in PubMed Central
sourceChecks.locator: §1, especially paragraphs 101–104, 117–127, 121–126; §2–3 and discussion §§4.2, including the population/speech-context limits of the experiments.
sourceChecks.scope: Peer-reviewed empirical research on Korean stops and measured laryngeal/acoustic cues; usable for the stop series only. It reports variation, contextual effects, and cue interaction; it does not support simplified claims that tense sounds always have zero air, “short/dry” release, or a hand-test.

sourceChecks.sourceTitle: Voice quality distinctions of the three-way stop contrast under prosodic strengthening in Korean
sourceChecks.organization: Jang, J., Kim, S., & Cho, T. (2024), Phonetics and Speech Sciences 16(1), 17–24
sourceChecks.locator: Abstract pp.17–18 (PDF p.0), lines 31–39 of the article text: 12 native Korean speakers, lenis/aspirated/fortis, voice-quality results and prosodic conditioning.
sourceChecks.scope: Open-access experimental study of the three-way stop contrast, with n=12 and prosodic conditioning. It does not justify generalized articulation instructions across speakers, onset/coda positions, or fricatives.

claimChecks.claimExcerpt: 1. **ㅅ (Consonante simple o laxa):** Se pronuncia de forma relajada, de manera muy similar a la "s" del español. El flujo de aire es suave y constante. 2. **ㅆ (Consonante tensa):** Se produce aumentando la presión del aire y la tensión en la lengua y los músculos de la boca. El sonido resultante es más fuerte, agudo y "seco".

claimChecks.claimExcerpt: Para un hispanohablante, la diferencia puede ser difícil de notar al principio porque en español solo tenemos un tipo de "s". Un error común es confundir la consonante tensa (**ㅆ**) con una aspirada (un sonido con mucho aire). La consonante tensa no busca expulsar aire, sino que busca "comprimir" el sonido mediante la tensión muscular.
